title: Share the warehouse stock between checkout threads

blocks.text: This practice starts from the previous one: `MeteredStock` is written, and it now also has a busy gauge, `inFlight()`, the number of calls that have started and not yet ended.

The checkout threads are moving onto the warehouse's `MapStock`, which was written for one thread. Nobody wants to change `MapStock` or the checkout code. Finish, in `src/main/java/practice/Stocks.java`:

items: `SynchronizedStock.level` and `SynchronizedStock.set`, a wrapper that makes any `Stock` safe to share between threads;
`shared(base)`, which wraps `base` for the checkout threads and returns the stock they call together with the `MeteredStock` the dashboard reads.

blocks.text: When you're done, the checkout threads can call the shared stock at the same time without corrupting it, a refused update (a negative count) doesn't stop other threads from using it, and the dashboard's busy gauge shows how many calls are working in the store right now, not how many are waiting their turn. About eight lines in total.

cases.says: the shared stock answers, refuses and counts as the store it wraps does
four threads setting levels at once through the shared stock leave every level as set
a read from one thread waits while another thread's update is inside the store
after the store throws on one thread's update, other threads can still call the shared stock
while one call is inside the store and another waits for it, the busy gauge reads 1

origin.section: Which Layer Holds the Lock Decides What the Metrics Measure

concepts: With a metrics decorator and a synchronizing one stacked, the order decides whether the metrics include time spent waiting for the lock.
A decorator that runs every call, reads included, under one lock makes any implementation safe to share.
